topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: I heard tell of a man who found his old bear at a yard sale, old and worn, the stuffing nearly done for. It must've brought back the days when life was simpler, when the biggest worry was a belly to fill or a bit of rain to spoil the wheat. He must've clung to that bear, rememberin' how his mother would mend it and how it kept him company when the nights were long and cold. I'd give a year's harvest to have such a thing, a piece of the past to hold onto. But we farmers, we’ve little for such keepsakes. Our hands are too rough from the plow, our hearts too worn from the weather. What good would it do, to want what cannot be had?
